newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Seardel aims for 42-48 cts 1996/7 eps.
newsitem.headline: Seardel aims for 42-48 cts 1996/7 eps.

text.p: Seardel Investment Corporation expects continued tough trading in the current financial year with earnings targeted at between 42 and 48 cents compared to 47.6 cents last year.
Chairman Aaron Searll said in his latest annual report that dividends were targeted to be between 12 and 14 cents compared to 9.25 cents for the year to June 30, 1996.

The turnover target was between 2.35 billion rand and 2.5 billion rand compared to 2.34 billion last year, while that for before tax income was 132 million rand to 142 million rand compared to 135.98 million rand.
"We expect again to be trading in a difficult climate," Searll said.
Volatile financial markets and "abnormally high interest rates may cause consumer spending to be at a lower level than last year," he said.

A review of financial strategies in the report said that despite slower consumer demand, "the group is well booked for the first half of financial 1997. Indications are that trading conditions will remain somewhat depressed in the short-term."
The group's capital expenditure programme was expected to cost about 85 million rand.
Searll said the results would also be affected by the recent seven day strike by clothing industry workers, which had been "unnecessary and could have been avoided".
He said the group would review its targets in February, when the interim results would be announced.
